column1: Content Calendar & Content Ideas
Content Ideas stores every problem you could make content about. Content Calendar tells you what you are actually creating and posting next. Ideas feed the Calendar.
How To Use The Content Ideas Tab
1. Open the Content Ideas tab and start a new row for every problem you find.
2. Write the problem plainly in the Problem column.
3. Paste how your ICP actually said it into Exact Language. Do not clean it up or make it sound professional.
4. Choose where you found it from the Source dropdown.
5. Count how many separate times that problem has come up and put the number in Frequency.
6. Sort the whole tab by Frequency, highest at the top. One mention could be a fluke, repeated mentions are signal.
7. Keep adding rows until you have at least 30 real problems.
8. Write the piece of content that problem turns into in the Content Idea column.
9. Choose the Format based on the idea itself, not on whatever you feel like making that week.
10. Set Status to Idea for everything you have not started.
11. When you pick one up, write a simple five-step solution under the problem, then set Status to In Progress.
12. Move Status to Scheduled once it is on the Content Calendar, and Published once it is live.
13. Paste the link into Published URL the day it goes out.
14. Remake your best ideas instead of hunting for new ones. Explain them more clearly, add better examples, change the format.
How To Use The Content Calendar Tab
1. Open this tab during your Weekly Planning Session, every Saturday or Sunday, for the week ahead.
2. Choose your primary source material for the week before you fill in a single row.
3. Decide how that source material gets repurposed across every platform you post on.
4. Add one row per post.
5. Fill in the Date, the Platform, and the Account or Channel it goes out from.
6. Copy the ICP Problem straight from your Content Ideas tab so every post traces back to a real problem.
7. Write what the post is actually about in the Topic column.
8. Choose the Format that needs to be produced.
9. Name the piece of source material it was repurposed from in Source Material.
10. Put a specific person in Assigned Person. Not 'the team'.
11. Set the Planned Posting Time so publishing is predictable instead of random.
12. Set Status so anyone can check progress without asking you.
13. Read down the week and confirm the content types are mixed, not stacked. Educational, proof, case studies, frameworks, Offer, opinions, tutorials, problem-and-solution.
14. Paste the link into Published URL once each post is live. This is what connects the Calendar to your Content Tracking Spreadsheet.
15. Duplicate this tab at the end of the session and rename it for the week it covers.
16. Plan every day of that week in advance, so nobody starts Monday wondering what to make.
